```luau
--!strict
-- UpgradeFx: client-only toast + corner label for upgrades. Sends nothing to the server.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Upgrades = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Upgrades", 10) :: ModuleScript)

local remote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("UpgradeBought", 10)
if not remote or not remote:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
	return
end

-- Theme (trimmed from house kit)
local Theme = {
	Ink = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38), Cream = Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232),
	Primary = Color3.fromRGB(255, 196, 41), Good = Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92),
	Info = Color3.fromRGB(64, 170, 255),
	Header = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, Body = Enum.Font.FredokaOne,
}

local function corner(gui: GuiObject, r: number?)
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, r or 12)
	c.Parent = gui
end

local function stroke(gui: GuiObject, px: number?, border: boolean?)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Thickness = px or 3
	s.Color = Theme.Ink
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = if border then Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border else Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	s.Parent = gui
end

local function tween(inst: Instance, t: number, props: { [string]: any }, style: Enum.EasingStyle?): Tween
	local tw = TweenService:Create(inst, TweenInfo.new(t, style or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), props)
	tw:Play()
	return tw
end

local function juiceScale(gui: GuiObject): UIScale
	local existing = gui:FindFirstChild("Juice")
	local s: UIScale
	if existing and existing:IsA("UIScale") then
		s = existing
	else
		s = Instance.new("UIScale")
		s.Name = "Juice"
		s.Parent = gui
	end
	return s
end

local function pop(gui: GuiObject, t: number?)
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 0
	tween(s, t or 0.3, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

local function punch(gui: GuiObject, amount: number?)
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 1 + (amount or 0.2)
	tween(s, 0.25, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui", 10)
if not playerGui then
	return
end

local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
gui.Name = "UpgradeFx"
gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
gui.DisplayOrder = 5
gui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
gui.Parent = playerGui

-- Toast list (top centre)
local toastList = Instance.new("Frame")
toastList.Name = "Toasts"
toastList.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(420, 200)
toastList.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
toastList.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 70)
toastList.BackgroundTransparency = 1
local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 8)
layout.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
layout.Parent = toastList
toastList.Parent = gui

local function toast(text: string, color: Color3?, seconds: number?)
	local count = 0
	for _, c in ipairs(toastList:GetChildren()) do
		if c:IsA("TextLabel") then
			count += 1
		end
	end
	if count >= 3 then
		return
	end
	local f = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	f.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(380, 48)
	f.BackgroundColor3 = color or Theme.Ink
	f.Text = text
	f.Font = Theme.Body
	f.TextScaled = true
	f.TextColor3 = Theme.Cream
	f.ZIndex = 20
	corner(f, 24)
	stroke(f, 3, true)
	stroke(f, 2.5)
	local pad = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	pad.PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, 8)
	pad.PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, 8)
	pad.Parent = f
	f.Parent = toastList
	pop(f, 0.25)
	task.delay(seconds or 2.2, function()
		if not f.Parent then
			return
		end
		local s = f:FindFirstChild("Juice")
		if s and s:IsA("UIScale") then
			tween(s, 0.2, { Scale = 0 }).Completed:Wait()
		end
		f:Destroy()
	end)
end
```

Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Do not give starting cash equal to the first upgrade's price. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. Make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup. Mark milestones such as the first cube, the first affordable upgrade and tier-ups with a distinct presentation.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

```luau
-- PriceBillboard: world price tag over a buy pad / shop item; green when affordable, red when not. Server or client.
-- Standalone (no Theme needed) so a server Script can paste it too.
local function priceBillboard(part: BasePart, title: string, price: number): (BillboardGui, (boolean) -> ())
	local bb = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	bb.Size, bb.StudsOffset = UDim2.fromScale(6, 2.2), Vector3.new(0, part.Size.Y / 2 + 2, 0)
	bb.AlwaysOnTop, bb.MaxDistance, bb.LightInfluence = false, 80, 0
	bb.Adornee = part
	local function text(t: string, y: number, h: number, color: Color3): TextLabel
		local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		l.Size, l.Position, l.BackgroundTransparency = UDim2.fromScale(1, h), UDim2.fromScale(0, y), 1
		l.Text, l.Font, l.TextScaled, l.TextColor3 = t, Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, true, color
		local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Thickness, s.Color = 3, Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
		s.Parent = l
		l.Parent = bb
		return l
	end
	text(title, 0, 0.45, Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232))
	local cost = text("$" .. tostring(price), 0.45, 0.55, Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64))
	bb.Parent = part
	local function setAffordable(ok: boolean)
		cost.TextColor3 = if ok then Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92) else Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64)
	end
	return bb, setAffordable -- client: call setAffordable(cash.Value >= price) on cash.Changed
end
```
